statement: Keep at least 2" air space between DuraTech and combustibles.
Chimney and connector diameter should equal the appliance flue outlet.
No more than two offsets (four elbows) per installation.
Elbows are fixed 15° or 30°; offsets steeper than 30° from vertical are not allowed.
At least one elbow strap per offset; installed between the two elbows.
Attic insulation shield is required whenever the chimney passes through an attic, insulated or not.
Firestop radiation shield is required at each floor/ceiling penetration that has no support box.
Every horizontal through-the-wall run uses a wall thimble with DuraTech pipe through it.
DuraTech pipe through a thimble extends 6" into the room past the interior wall.
Wall straps are required at 8 ft intervals along an exterior run.
An extended roof bracket is required once 5 ft or more of chimney stands above the roof penetration.
Add another roof bracket for each additional 5 ft.
A storm collar is required with every roof flashing. Seal with 500°F non-hardening sealant.
Chimney extends at least 3 ft above where it passes through the roof.
Chimney is at least 2 ft higher than any part of the building within the horizontal distance below.
Horizontal radius used for the 2 ft rule.
Straight vertical system height above appliance outlet, at sea level.
Elbows, a tee, or higher elevation call for roughly 30-60% more height.
Sites at or above this elevation count as high altitude, where appliance manuals commonly call for a taller chimney.
Route the chimney inside the building when possible; exterior runs draft worse and build more creosote.
Follow local code and have the finished system inspected by a certified professional.
Factory-built chimneys are installed per their listing and the manufacturer instructions; the listing governs clearances.

statement: Keep at least 2" clearance between EXCEL and combustibles, except inside factory-built supports certified for less.
The chimney should be the size recommended by the appliance manufacturer.
No more than four elbows (two offsets) in one installation.
Offsets use 15° or 30° insulated elbows; 45° elbows are certified for Canada only.
An offset support (EOS) or roof support must be installed above each offset (two elbows), anywhere on the vertical run above it.
Where the chimney enters an insulated attic, the support or radiation shield needs a storm collar on top so insulation cannot fall into the air space.
EXCEL has no pass-through shield; use a radiation shield (ERS) at each floor and ceiling.
The horizontal chimney section extends at least 4" into the room past the finished interior wall.
Install another wall support at 8 ft intervals up the wall.
If the chimney extends more than 5 ft above the roof, secure it with a roof brace (ERB).
The EXCEL instructions call for a roof brace above 5 ft and give no spacing for more than one.
Every EXCEL flashing comes with its storm collar; seal it to the chimney with silicone.
A roof radiation shield (ERRS) is required with some roof support and outside chase installations.
The chimney extends at least 3 ft above where it passes through the roof.
The chimney is at least 2 ft higher than any wall, roof or building within 10 ft.
Horizontal distance used for the 2 ft rule.
The EXCEL instructions do not cover decorative shrouds; ask ICC before fitting one.
The EXCEL instructions give no minimum chimney height for draft; the appliance manual's figure applies.
The EXCEL instructions give no height allowance for elbows, a tee or altitude; the appliance manual's table applies.
If possible install an interior chimney: it performs better than an exterior one, which can draft poorly and build creosote quickly in cold climates.
Contact local building or fire officials about restrictions and installation inspection in your area.
With a factory-built fireplace, the chimney and fireplace are tested as one system: follow the fireplace instructions.
Seal the chimney where it leaves the chase top with a storm collar.
For chase installations, the chimney extends at least 8" above the top of the chase.
